If $D$ is the finite region enclosed by the curves $y=\frac{1}{8}{x}^{2}$ and $y=\sqrt{x},$ as shown above, then ${∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA=$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's represent $D$ as a type I region. To determine the lower and upper functions, we draw a vertical arrow through the region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14150437/assets/1ab9ae94853a0d161c74aa8d79c47a38f0b0453e0ece320c367098794d5bcb59.png)

As a result, we get

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 4,\,\frac{1}{8}{x}^{2}\le y\le \sqrt{x}\}.
$$

Therefore, we can express the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{{x}^{2}/8}^{\sqrt{x}}f(x,y)\,dy\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}[{\int }_{{x}^{2}/8}^{\sqrt{x}}f(x,y)\,dy]dx\end{aligned}
$$
